subject: Physics
question: State Newton's second law of motion and explain why a heavier object has greater inertia.
model_answer: Newton's second law states that the net force acting on an object equals its mass multiplied by its acceleration (F = ma). Inertia is an object's resistance to any change in its state of motion. Because inertial mass is the property that resists acceleration, a heavier object has greater inertia and needs a larger force to produce the same acceleration.
